q: In what year did The University of Texas at Austin first open its doors?
fact: UT opened on September 15, 1883.

q: What kind of animal is Bevo, the UT mascot?
options: A free-roaming North American wild Mustang
fact: Bevo is a Texas Longhorn steer, and the name debuted in 1916.

q: What are the University of Texas at Austin's official colors?
fact: The Tower glows burnt orange after major Longhorn victories.

q: Roughly how tall is the iconic UT Austin Tower?
fact: UT's own 'Tower by the Numbers' lists 307 feet and 27 floors.

q: In what year was the 'Hook 'em Horns' hand sign introduced at UT Austin?
fact: Head cheerleader Harley Clark introduced the sign in 1955.

q: 'The Eyes of Texas' is sung to the tune of which song?
options: I've Been Working on the Railroad
fact: The Eyes of Texas lyrics date to around 1903.

q: What is the nickname of the UT Austin Longhorn Band?
options: The Lone Star All-American Marching Band
fact: Big Bertha, the band's giant bass drum, is part of the Showband.

q: About how wide (in diameter) is Big Bertha, the UT Longhorn Band's giant bass drum?
fact: Big Bertha is billed as the world's largest bass drum.

q: Which UT Austin research library houses a Gutenberg Bible?
fact: The Ransom Center's copy is a complete Gutenberg Bible printed in the 1450s.

q: The world's oldest surviving photograph is kept at which UT Austin institution?
fact: The photo is Nicephore Niepce's 'View from the Window at Le Gras' from about 1826.

q: The replica Oval Office at the LBJ Presidential Library on the UT Austin campus is built to what scale?
fact: The replica Oval Office is built at 7/8 scale.

q: Which artist designed the chapel-like building 'Austin' at UT Austin's Blanton Museum of Art?
fact: 'Austin' (2018) is the only building Ellsworth Kelly designed.

q: Which group branded '13-0' onto Bevo I in a famous 1917 rivalry prank?
fact: A&M students branded Bevo in 1917; Texas students then altered the brand to read BEVO.

q: Which Oscar-winning actor and UT alumnus is a professor of practice at UT Austin?
options: Ethan Hawke (acclaimed film actor and Austin native)
fact: McConaughey, a UT alumnus, won Best Actor for Dallas Buyers Club.

q: Which First Lady earned a journalism degree from UT Austin in 1934?
options: Rosalynn Carter (First Lady and mental health advocate)
fact: Lady Bird Johnson earned a journalism degree in 1934, after a history degree in 1933.

q: Which tech founder started his computer company from a UT Austin dorm room?
fact: Michael Dell started his company in his UT dorm room in 1984.

q: Which Longhorn running back won the Heisman Trophy in 1977?
fact: Earl Campbell was Texas's first Heisman Trophy winner.

q: In the January 2006 Rose Bowl, which team did Texas beat to win the 2005 national title?
fact: Vince Young led Texas to a 41-38 win over USC.

q: How many consensus football national championships does Texas officially claim?
fact: Texas's consensus titles came in 1963, 1969, 1970 and 2005.

q: In what year did Texas officially join the SEC?
fact: Texas and Oklahoma joined the SEC together on July 1, 2024.

q: In what year did ESPN launch the Longhorn Network for Texas?
fact: The Longhorn Network launched in September 2011 under a 20-year ESPN deal.

q: How many NCAA baseball national championships has Texas won (through 2026)?
fact: Texas won its titles in 1949, 1950, 1975, 1983, 2002 and 2005.

q: The Longhorns' football stadium was renamed in 1996 in honor of which legendary three-time national championship-winning head coach?
options: Tom Landry (hall of fame Dallas Cowboys head coach)
fact: Royal won three national titles at Texas: 1963, 1969 and 1970.

q: What was the nickname of UT's old Frank Erwin Center arena?
fact: The Moody Center replaced the Erwin Center in 2022.

q: What is the nickname for UT's original campus site?
fact: The name comes from the roughly 40-acre plot of the original campus site.

q: Which Austin creek runs along the east side of the UT campus?
fact: Waller Creek is named for Edwin Waller, who laid out the city of Austin.

q: Guadalupe Street along the west edge of the UT campus goes by what nickname?
fact: The Drag is lined with shops and restaurants right beside campus.

q: UT Austin operates which famous observatory in the Davis Mountains of West Texas?
fact: McDonald Observatory sits near Fort Davis in West Texas.

q: The Texas Advanced Computing Center (TACC) is best known for hosting what?
fact: TACC has housed supercomputers such as Stampede and Frontera.

q: How many bells are in the Kniker Carillon of the UT Austin Tower?
fact: UT says the heaviest bell weighs 7,350 pounds and the lightest 20 pounds.

q: Which architect designed the UT Tower and much of the campus plan?
fact: Paul Cret was a French-born architect based in Philadelphia.

q: When Texas wins a national championship, what does the UT Tower light up with?
fact: The Tower shows a lit-up No. 1 after Texas wins a national championship.

q: Which student service organization takes care of Bevo today?
fact: The Silver Spurs were formed in 1937 to care for Bevo.

q: What is the name of UT Austin's student newspaper?
fact: The Daily Texan is a student-run newspaper.

q: What is the name of UT Austin's yearbook?
fact: The first Cactus yearbook was published in 1894.

q: What is UT's alumni association called?
fact: Texas Exes is the alumni association of UT Austin.

q: Which legendary CBS news anchor attended UT Austin?
fact: Cronkite worked at The Daily Texan before leaving UT in 1935 to pursue journalism.

q: Which 'Charlie's Angels' star attended UT Austin?
fact: Farrah Fawcett attended UT Austin before becoming a star of Charlie's Angels.

q: The Texas State Capitol, just south of the UT Austin campus, is how tall compared to the U.S. Capitol?
fact: The Texas Capitol is about 302.64 feet tall versus about 288 feet for the U.S. Capitol.

q: Which of these is UT Austin's well-known slogan?
options: What starts here changes the world.
fact: 'What starts here changes the world' is UT Austin's well-known slogan.

q: Which giant pterosaur has a replica hanging in UT's Texas Science & Natural History Museum?
fact: Quetzalcoatlus fossils were found in Big Bend National Park.

q: In what year did Bevo I first appear as the UT mascot?
fact: Bevo I first appeared at the Thanksgiving 1916 game against Texas A&M.

q: Who was the head cheerleader credited with creating the 'Hook 'em' sign?
fact: Harley Clark made the sign at a 1955 pep rally.

q: In what year did Texas Memorial Stadium first open?
fact: The stadium was dedicated in 1924 as a memorial to Texans who died in World War I.

q: How many floors does the UT Austin Tower have?
fact: UT lists 27 floors in the Tower, plus extra stairs to the clock and bells.

q: The Littlefield Fountain on the UT campus honors those who served in which conflict?
fact: The fountain, dedicated in 1933, honors those who served in World War I.

q: What does 'PCL' stand for at UT Austin?
fact: PCL is the library on campus that most students just call 'PCL'.

q: The Texas-Oklahoma football rivalry game awards which trophy?
fact: The Golden Hat goes to the winner of the Texas-Oklahoma Red River Rivalry.

q: The UT Tower is part of which campus building?
fact: The Tower rises from the Main Building.
